children: By Mike Scarcella
A fight over attorney loyalties has erupted in a lawsuit over the use of photographs to train AI technology, threatening law firm Crowell & Moring's continued role in the case.

Online art gallery DeviantArt asked a federal judge in Los Angeles on Wednesday to disqualify Crowell & Moring from representing automotive photography company Evox in the lawsuit, saying the firm previously advised defendant DeviantArt and its parent company on AI and other matters.
DeviantArt said in a

that Crowell advised its parent company Wix.com and its subsidiaries from 2022 through 2026 on AI litigation, AI regulation and copyright issues. The company said the firm also advised DeviantArt on its DreamUp AI image-generation service.
"Crowell's conflict is substantive, not merely technical," DeviantArt told the court. It said the firm's prior work allowed it to acquire "material confidential information" about the company.
Crowell had no immediate comment. Evox and Wix.com did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Washington, DC-based Crowell employs nearly 700 lawyers and is known for its litigation and regulatory work.
Evox
DeviantArt and several AI companies in July, alleging they violated copyright law by using its photographs to train artificial intelligence models.
DeviantArt, founded in 2000, operates an online community for artists and offers an AI image-generation service called DreamUp. It is a subsidiary of the Israeli company Wix.com.

Crowell advised Wix.com on a range of matters from 2022 until this year, according to DeviantArt, including advice on “core products and intellectual property strategies” related to DreamUp and its launch.
In a September letter cited in the filing, Crowell's general counsel said the firm had not performed work for Wix or its subsidiaries since 2024 and had no conflict of interest.
DeviantArt counters that Crowell never formally or informally terminated its relationship with Wix.com or any of its subsidiaries, including DeviantArt.
The company also argues that “a pause in billable work does not convert a client into a former client.”
The case is Evox Productions LLC v. Stability AI et al, US District Court for the Central District of California, No. 2:26-cv-07201-CAS-RAO.
For plaintiff: Kent Goss and Valerie Goo of Crowell & Moring
For DeviantArt: Rachel Fertig and Gina Durham of DLA Piper, and Edward McIntyre
